text:
tess: heads-up: encountered a weird onboarding hiccup — the sample-rerank app got back mismatched embedding lengths after an auth-retry + batching helper path. node-sdk repro.

omar: can you summarize what you saw? dims, field names, model id?

tess: sequence: send batch of 4, token refresh happens mid-flight, retry re-enqueues items. Response arrives with 8 vectors (duplicates) and field named "embedding" (singular) instead of the documented "embeddings". Also some hosts returned 1024-d vectors while others returned 1536-d even though model alias was open-embed-1536.

sam: that sounds like three issues colliding: missing per-item idempotency keys (duplicates), gateway/handler version skew (field rename), and model artifact mismatch (dim projection). Which SDK/version?

tess: node-sdk@0.11.4 with batching-helper@1.3.2. rust and python samples didn't show duplicates in their runs.

anya: log excerpt from gateway: [2026-05-12T15:02:10Z] recv POST /embeddings items=4 client=sample-rerank
[2026-05-12T15:02:10Z] auth refresh start client=sample-rerank token=expiring
[2026-05-12T15:02:11Z] retry from sdk id=retry-13 reenqueue batch=sh-42
[2026-05-12T15:02:11Z] batch merge id=sh-42 items=8 handler=embed-handler-v3
[2026-05-12T15:02:11Z] dispatch to embed-fastpath-hostA proj=1024
[2026-05-12T15:02:11Z] fallback to embed-compat-hostB proj=1536 field_map=embeddings->embedding

tess: note the field_map entry and the projection mismatch.

omar: I suspect routing allowed a mixed handler set to process the merged batch. The fastpath host advertised a 1024 projection (old quantized artifact) while compat host had 1536. If the response chosen comes from different handlers or the batch was split across hosts, the sampleapp's merge logic can map indices incorrectly.

sam: short-term mitigations: (1) sample apps should set per-item idempotency keys (uuid per text) so retried items don't duplicate; (2) SDKs should add a test that simulates token expiry and asserts no duplicates; (3) gateway should normalize response field names to canonical "embeddings" before returning to clients.

anya: I'll open INFRA ticket to pin routing to handler versions for the duration of a merged batch. Also adding a compatibility shim in the gateway to rewrite "embedding" -> "embeddings" and to validate vector length == requested model dim if model_version is pinned.

omar: can we also update batching-helper to honor explicit idempotency_key fields and dedupe at enqueue? I've seen helpers rewrite fields for fastpath to reduce payload; that rewriting should be reversible.

sam: agreed. I'll add a parity integration test in devex/integration that creates a run where token expires, retry happens, and the batcher merges; assert final response length == input count and vector dims match expected for the pinned model. Put this in node + rust + python CI.

tess: quick repro gist attached: https://gist.github.com/redwood/embed-retry-dim-repro. It has a tiny node script that simulates token expiry by using a short-lived test token.

ci-bot: deploy: batching-helper 1.3.3 -> 1.3.4 (honor idempotency_key + avoid irreversible field renames). rollout to dev started.

sam: release note blurb: Node SDK <0.12 may re-enqueue items on auth-retry with batching helper leading to duplicate embeddings; upgrade recommended. Gateway will normalize legacy field names and infra will pin handler versions during merges.

omar: follow-ups: 1) runtime to expose model_dim in capability handshake so gateway can sanity-check responses, 2) docs: add explicit API contract for "embeddings" field and vector dim expectations, 3) SDKs: centralize batching helper behavior in shared library for parity.

tess: thanks all — will monitor dev after staging deploy. If anyone sees singular "embedding" in the wild please paste request id in #devex so we can trace.
